menu_simplification_manifest_rule.statement: Menus must stay simple; any feature common to 2D/3D/4D menus must live in the shared settings menu unless a very strong mode-specific reason is documented, with custom topology editing owned by the Explorer Playground.

banned_python_literals.message: settings_hub_model.py must not hardcode settings section header ownership; use config/menu/structure.json
settings_hub_model.py must not hardcode settings section filters; use config/menu/structure.json
settings_hub_model.py must not hardcode settings footer row ownership; use config/menu/structure.json
settings_hub_model.py must not hardcode top-level settings headers; use config/menu/structure.json

godot_settings_externalization_contract.statement: Every Godot presentation parameter, its default, exactly-one semantic owner, accessibility classification, and runtime applicability must be declared in the checked-in shell settings registry; runtime code may map validated preset values but must not introduce a second setting default. Persistent user choices must be written only to the separate user-data JSON store.

directives.statement: Plan restructuring or behaviour work with acceptance criteria.
Update owning design and active backlog; use CURRENT_STATE only for handoff.
Run the canonical local/full verification required by the change.
Report LOC delta and prefer reduction for non-feature refactors.
Use quiet verification output except during diagnosis.
Use patch edits for local changes and deterministic rewrites for broad changes.
Preserve UTF-8 and reject literal escape artifacts.
Check encoding, escape artifacts, and focused lint after rewrites.
Run focused checks before serialized full gates.
Use the repository-managed interpreter when available.
Switch method after a rejected patch attempt.
Do not claim completion before every acceptance criterion passes.
Prefer additive staged migration over destructive replacement.
Report the final staged-migration delta and remaining blockers.

rules.description: Prefer stdlib or existing repo helpers for parsing and validation rather than ad-hoc local variants.

Use existing project config, path, and JSON helper flows before introducing custom wrappers.
Prefer stdlib functional utilities over ad-hoc rewrites for common collection transforms.
